stated.text: The app is a small local project-room app titled "Roundtable" (the page shows and is titled Roundtable).
The app is served by server.js.
The server runs on Node.js.
The app has no npm dependencies (none declared in any package.json, no node_modules needed).
The server listens on the port given in the PORT environment variable.
When PORT is not set, the server listens on port 3000.
GET / serves the app.
The app has a light, Gemini-like look and feel.
The app starts with one room, named Launch plan.
The Launch plan room is seeded with a realistic conversation.
The seeded conversation contains at least one message from Maya, a person.
The seeded conversation contains at least one message from Theo, a person.
The seeded conversation contains at least one message from Scribe, an agent.
Scribe is clearly identified as a demonstration agent.
The current user is Maya.
A region named Conversation contains the messages.
Each message in the Conversation region is an article.
Each message article shows its author.
Each message article shows its person/agent identity.
Each message article shows its time.
Each message article is accessibly named Message from Maya, Message from Theo or Message from Scribe using its actual author.
There is a textbox named Message for composing a message.
There is a Send button for sending the composed message.
Pressing Enter in the Message textbox sends the message.
Pressing Shift+Enter in the Message textbox inserts a newline.
Whitespace-only text is ignored: sending it adds no message.
Sending preserves multiline text (line breaks are kept in the sent message).
Sending clears that draft from the Message textbox.
Sending a message containing @Scribe calls the local POST /api/agent endpoint.
That call sends the JSON body {"text": <the complete sent text>}.
POST /api/agent is deterministic and returns exactly {"text": "Demo reply: " followed by that text}.
POST /api/agent rejects whitespace-only text with HTTP 400.
POST /api/agent uses no external service.
While awaiting the agent reply, the app shows a working state with role status.
On a failed response, the app shows an alert.
On a failed response, the app shows a Retry Scribe button.
Retry Scribe retries the agent reply.
Retrying does not duplicate the person message.
The URL /?empty=1 starts an empty conversation.
The empty conversation shows useful guidance.
In the empty conversation, sending still works.
The ?empty=1 fixture control is not a normal UI feature.
A visible Use dark appearance button switches the appearance.
After switching, that button becomes Use light appearance.
Use light appearance switches the appearance back.
At a 320px narrow browser width, reading and composing stay usable without page-level horizontal scrolling.
At a 390px narrow browser width, reading and composing stay usable without page-level horizontal scrolling.
At a 1440px wide browser width, reading and composing stay usable without page-level horizontal scrolling.
State can live in the current browser session.
The state rules are in a module that the app uses.
node:test tests under test/ cover those state rules.
Those tests run with node --test.
This first delivery has one room.
This first delivery has one local agent.
This first delivery has no accounts.
This first delivery has no file sharing.
This first delivery has no canvases.
This first delivery uses no external services.

unstated.text: Which text counts as containing @Scribe: letter case (@scribe, @SCRIBE), position (start, middle, end, on its own line), punctuation around it (@Scribe, or (@Scribe)), longer words or addresses (@Scribes, a@Scribe, me@Scribe.com, @@Scribe), and more than one occurrence in one message.
unstated.why: Maya will type the mention in different ways; a mention that silently gets no reply makes the agent look broken, a false match triggers a reply she did not ask for, and the maintainer needs one stable rule to test.
unstated.probe: From a fresh session on /, send each of these on its own and record whether POST /api/agent fires (network panel) and, if so, its JSON text: hello @Scribe; hello @scribe; hello @SCRIBE; @Scribe; ping @Scribe now; @Scribe, can you summarise?; (@Scribe); see @Scribes; a@Scribe; mail me@Scribe.com; @@Scribe; line1, newline, @Scribe, newline, line2; and @Scribe twice in one message.
unstated.fine_answers: A case-sensitive @Scribe match anywhere in the text, including with trailing punctuation, or a case-insensitive match; treating @Scribes or a@Scribe as a mention or requiring a word boundary are both fine if consistent. More than one occurrence sends one POST with the complete sent text.

unstated.text: A send that does not contain @Scribe adds Maya's message and makes no call to POST /api/agent.
unstated.why: Most messages in a project room are ordinary talk; the operator needs them to appear without an agent call or reply.
unstated.probe: On /, count the Conversation articles. Type I will bring the agenda (no @Scribe) and click Send; record the new article's author, person/agent identity, time and accessible name, and whether any POST /api/agent fired. Repeat with Enter on a fresh draft.
unstated.fine_answers: Exactly one new article from Maya, shown as a person, and no POST /api/agent. Calling the endpoint for every send, or dropping the message, is not fine.

unstated.text: Shift+Enter only inserts a newline and never also sends the draft; the draft stays until Enter or Send.
unstated.why: Someone using Shift+Enter to keep writing a multiline message must not have a half-written draft sent.
unstated.probe: Focus Message, type line one, press Shift+Enter, type line two and stop. Record whether an article was added, whether POST /api/agent was called, and whether the textbox holds both lines. Then press Enter and check one message contains both lines.
unstated.fine_answers: Shift+Enter inserts a newline and sends nothing; one message with both lines appears after Enter.

unstated.text: Where and how the Scribe reply appears: as a new Conversation article from Scribe with agent identity, a time and the accessible name Message from Scribe, showing the exact response text, placed after the person message that mentioned it.
unstated.why: The customer mentions Scribe to get a reply; a working POST with no visible, correctly attributed answer leaves the operator with nothing, and maintainer tests need to know what success looks like.
unstated.probe: On /, type Please summarize this, Shift+Enter, @Scribe and press Enter. Record the POST /api/agent response body. When the wait ends, record every new article: full text, author, identity, time, accessible name and position. Compare the shown reply with the response text, including the Demo reply: prefix and the newline. Count Maya articles for that send.
unstated.fine_answers: Maya's message appears once; the exact response text appears once, attributed to Scribe as an agent, after her message, preferably as an article named Message from Scribe with a time. Another clearly attributed visible reply surface showing the exact text is also acceptable. Hiding the reply or replacing Maya's message is not fine.

unstated.text: Which outcomes count as a failed agent response (network error, HTTP 4xx/5xx, a non-JSON or malformed body, a server that never answers) and how long the app waits before treating a reply as failed.
unstated.why: If a failure is not recognised, Maya sees the working state forever with no Retry Scribe; an operator needs failures to surface.
unstated.probe: Load /, then stop the server and send @Scribe hi; note whether an alert and Retry Scribe appear. Restart, and using devtools request blocking or an override make POST /api/agent return 500, then a non-JSON 200 body, then never respond; note what the UI shows for each after 30 s and after 2 min.
unstated.fine_answers: Network errors and non-2xx responses shown as failures; a timeout from a few seconds to about a minute, or no timeout but a way to cancel. Limiting failure to network and server errors is also fine. A working state that never ends without recourse is not fine.

unstated.text: What the failure alert is and says (an in-page role alert or a browser dialog, and its wording), and what happens to the alert and Retry Scribe after a successful retry, after a second failure, and when a later @Scribe message is sent while a failure is shown.
unstated.why: Maya needs to know what failed and when it is fixed; stale alerts, a modal dialog blocking the button, or several Retry buttons attached to the wrong messages mislead her.
unstated.probe: Block /api/agent and send @Scribe one; record whether the alert is in-page or a dialog, its text, and whether Retry Scribe can be used while the alert is up. Click Retry Scribe with the endpoint still blocked: count alerts and Retry buttons. Unblock and click Retry Scribe: check the alert and button are gone and exactly one Maya message and one reply exist. With one failure showing, send @Scribe two and note the alerts and buttons.
unstated.fine_answers: Any wording saying the reply failed; in-page alert or a dialog (with the button usable after dismissing it). One alert per failed reply or one shared alert; the alert and Retry Scribe clear after success; a second failure shows them again with still one person message.

unstated.text: What Retry Scribe resends and which message it targets: the original complete sent text of the message whose reply failed, not the current unsent draft or a later message.
unstated.why: A retry that posts the current draft or targets the wrong failed message gives a reply to text Maya never sent there.
unstated.probe: Fail the reply to once @Scribe. Type a different unsent draft in Message, click Retry Scribe, and record the POST JSON text. Then fail two mentions in a row (@Scribe A, @Scribe B), click each Retry Scribe and record which text each POST carries and where each reply lands.
unstated.fine_answers: Retry posts the original complete sent text of the failed message and leaves the draft untouched; with two failures, each retry targets its own message (or one retry covers the latest, if stated).

unstated.text: Activating Send or Retry Scribe twice quickly (double click, repeated Enter) does not produce two person messages, two identical agent calls or two Scribe replies.
unstated.why: A duplicate agent reply is the agent-side twin of the duplicate person message the request forbids; an unresponsive-feeling button invites a second click.
unstated.probe: Throttle the network (devtools Slow 3G). Double-click Send for twice @Scribe and count person articles and POSTs. Block /api/agent, send @Scribe once, unblock, double-click Retry Scribe quickly; count Scribe replies after it settles.
unstated.fine_answers: Send and Retry Scribe disabled or hidden while pending, or a guard that ignores the second activation; exactly one person message and one reply result.

unstated.text: What happens when Maya sends another message, or another @Scribe message, while a Scribe reply is still pending: whether the composer stays usable, and in what order messages and replies are placed.
unstated.why: Maya keeps working while Scribe is thinking; replies landing out of order or attached to the wrong message confuse the conversation, and a blocked composer stops her.
unstated.probe: Delay /api/agent (Slow 3G or an override). Send @Scribe first, then immediately @Scribe second and plain note. Wait for all replies; record the order of messages and replies and whether the working state and Send stayed usable throughout.
unstated.fine_answers: The composer stays usable and each reply follows its own message in send order; or further sends are blocked or queued with a visible state. Silently dropping a send is not fine.

unstated.text: What the working state says, where it appears, and that it is present for the whole wait and gone once a reply or the failure alert is shown, including during and after Retry Scribe.
unstated.why: role status is what a waiting person, including a screen-reader user, has while Scribe has not answered; a status left up after the outcome contradicts what is shown.
unstated.probe: Slow POST /api/agent. Send draft the note @Scribe; while it is open, record the role status element's text and position relative to Conversation. After the reply, check the status is gone. Provoke a failure: record the status during the wait and after the alert. Click Retry Scribe and record the status during the second wait and after its result.
unstated.fine_answers: Any short visible status text, inside or next to Conversation, present for the whole wait and cleared once a reply or the alert is shown. Skipping it for an instant response is arguable; leaving it up after the outcome is not fine.

unstated.text: Which characters count as whitespace-only (spaces, tabs, newlines, a non-breaking space, the empty string) in the composer and at the endpoint, and whether an ignored draft stays in the Message textbox.
unstated.why: Enter on a blank line is a normal slip; the operator needs to know nothing was added and whether the typed text is still there, and the endpoint's 400 depends on the same set of characters.
unstated.probe: In Message, submit three spaces, then only a newline (Shift+Enter then Enter), then only a tab, then only a non-breaking space; for each record articles added, any POST /api/agent, and whether the textbox still holds the draft. Separately POST /api/agent with text set to three spaces, a newline, a tab, space-newline-space, an empty string and a non-breaking space, and record each status and body.
unstated.fine_answers: Spaces, tabs and newlines are whitespace: no message, no agent call, and HTTP 400 at the endpoint. Keeping or clearing the ignored draft are both fine. A non-breaking space treated either way is fine. An empty string may get 400 or another 4xx.

unstated.text: Whether the Send button is disabled or stays active while the draft is empty or whitespace-only.
unstated.why: Users need to see why nothing happened when they press Send; the request only says such text is ignored.
unstated.probe: Open /, leave Message empty and check the Send button's disabled state; click it. Type three spaces, check again and click. Confirm no message is added and no error appears.
unstated.fine_answers: Disabled while empty or whitespace-only, or enabled and ignoring the click; both fine as long as nothing is sent.

unstated.text: Whether leading and trailing whitespace and internal blank lines of a non-empty message are kept exactly or trimmed, consistently in the shown message, the POST body and the Demo reply: echo.
unstated.why: The exact echo is a stated contract, so the maintainer must know what the sent text is; pasted notes often carry indents or trailing newlines, and Maya may notice stray blank lines.
unstated.probe: Send two spaces, hello, newline, newline, world, two spaces (no @Scribe) and compare the article text with what was typed. Then send two spaces, hello @Scribe, newline, next, Shift+Enter twice; compare the Maya article, the POST JSON text and the text after Demo reply: in the response.
unstated.fine_answers: Kept exactly as typed, or only the outer ends trimmed with internal blank lines kept; the shown message, the POST text and the echo must use the same string. Dropping an internal blank line is not fine.

unstated.text: What POST /api/agent answers for a body that is not valid JSON, has no text field, has a non-string text (number, null, array), or has a wrong content type; and that the server stays up afterwards.
unstated.why: An operator or the next maintainer calling the endpoint by hand needs a clear client error, not a crash, a hung request or a 500 that kills the server process.
unstated.probe: Start the server. Run curl -i -X POST localhost:3000/api/agent -d 'not json'; then with -H 'Content-Type: application/json' and bodies '{}', '{"text":42}', '{"text":null}', '{"text":["a"]}'. Record each status and body, then curl -i localhost:3000/ to confirm the server still answers.
unstated.fine_answers: HTTP 400 (or another 4xx, e.g. 415 for wrong content type) with a short error for each malformed case; extra fields may be ignored. A 500 that crashes the server or a request that never answers is not fine.

unstated.text: The HTTP status, Content-Type and body shape of POST /api/agent responses: on success, and the body of the whitespace-only HTTP 400.
unstated.why: The front end, the node:test module and any later consumer parse these responses; a 400 with an HTML body or a success without a JSON content type can break parsing.
unstated.probe: curl -i -X POST localhost:3000/api/agent -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"Hi @Scribe"}' twice; record status, Content-Type and body and compare the two bodies. Repeat with '{"text":"   "}' and record status and body.
unstated.fine_answers: Success is 200 or 201 with application/json (or another JSON type) and exactly {"text": "Demo reply: Hi @Scribe"}, identical each time. The 400 body may be empty, plain text or JSON with an error field.

unstated.text: How other methods and unknown paths are answered: GET /api/agent, PUT /api/agent, an unknown path such as /nope.
unstated.why: An operator expects a 404 or 405 rather than the app page or a crash on every path.
unstated.probe: curl -i localhost:3000/api/agent; curl -i -X PUT localhost:3000/api/agent; curl -i localhost:3000/nope. Record statuses and bodies, then confirm GET / still serves the app.
unstated.fine_answers: 404 or 405 for unknown routes and methods; serving the app page for unknown non-API paths is tolerable if stated. A crash or hang is not fine.

unstated.text: Whether the server serves files outside the app's public assets, such as server.js, test files or files outside the project folder through path traversal.
unstated.why: A hand-written static handler can expose source or arbitrary files on the machine to anyone who can reach the port.
unstated.probe: curl -i --path-as-is localhost:3000/../server.js; curl -i --path-as-is 'localhost:3000/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd'; curl -i localhost:3000/test/. Record statuses and bodies.
unstated.fine_answers: 404 or 403 for anything outside the served assets; serving app assets including the shared state module is fine. Serving files outside the project folder is not fine.

unstated.text: Which network interface the server binds to (localhost only or all interfaces), given the request calls it a local app.
unstated.why: Someone running it on a laptop on shared Wi-Fi may not expect the room to be reachable by others on the network.
unstated.probe: Start the server and run lsof -nP -iTCP:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN (or netstat); note whether it listens on 127.0.0.1 or *. From another machine on the network, try curl http://<host-ip>:3000/.
unstated.fine_answers: Either 127.0.0.1 or all interfaces is acceptable for a local demo; documenting which is enough.

unstated.text: What happens when the port is already in use or PORT is not a valid number.
unstated.why: The operator needs a readable message and a non-zero exit, not a silent hang or a stack trace to decode.
unstated.probe: Start one server on 3000, then run node server.js again; note the output and exit code. Stop it and run PORT=abc node server.js; note what it does.
unstated.fine_answers: A clear error and non-zero exit, or falling back to the default for an invalid PORT; a raw EADDRINUSE stack trace is tolerable but less useful. A silent hang is not fine.

unstated.text: Message text is shown as plain text, not interpreted as HTML (in person messages and in the Scribe reply).
unstated.why: Maya pasting code or angle brackets expects to see exactly what she typed; interpreting it as HTML loses text and lets typed content run script.
unstated.probe: Open /, send bold & @Scribe. Check that the person message and the Scribe reply show the literal characters, with no bold, no broken image and no alert dialog.
unstated.fine_answers: Plain text; a deliberate, stated safe markdown subset is also fine. Script running or markup rendered from typed text is not fine.

unstated.text: A send updates the current page in place rather than navigating or reloading it.
unstated.why: A reload can drop a session-only transcript, repeat the seeded conversation, or abandon an in-flight POST /api/agent.
unstated.probe: Type stay put and click Send; watch for a document reload, a flash of the original seed or a scroll reset, and record the resulting articles. Repeat with Enter. Then send stay @Scribe and check the working state and reply complete without a reload.
unstated.fine_answers: Conversation updates in place. A reload that still shows the sent message once and completes one agent reply is also acceptable. A reload that loses the send or duplicates the seed is not fine.

unstated.text: Which state survives a reload, a new tab and a new browser session: messages, appearance and an unsent draft; and whether two open tabs share updates.
unstated.why: Someone who refreshes after writing, or toggles dark appearance and comes back, needs to know what is kept; a tester expects a predictable reset, and the maintainer must know which store is used.
unstated.probe: On /, send keep me, activate Use dark appearance, and leave not sent yet in Message. Reload the same tab; record messages, appearance, button label and draft. Open / in a new tab and in a private window, and after quitting the browser; record the same. With two tabs open, send in one and check the other.
unstated.fine_answers: Page memory only, sessionStorage for the tab, or persistence beyond the session are all fine if consistent; losing an unsent draft on reload is fine; two tabs may share or stay independent. The appearance button label must match the appearance shown after reload. Server accounts or profiles are out of scope.

unstated.text: How /?empty=1 relates to session state and to a later GET /: whether stored messages override the empty start, whether the fixture disturbs the seeded room, and what the empty page shows (room name, @Scribe still calling the agent).
unstated.why: A tester switching between / and /?empty=1 needs each URL to start as described; leaking state between them makes the fixture unreliable.
unstated.probe: Open /, send seeded extra. Open /?empty=1 in the same tab: check the conversation is empty with guidance and note whether Launch plan is shown. Send from empty, then hello @Scribe and check POST /api/agent runs and the reply appears. Go to /: record which messages show. Reload /?empty=1: empty again or holding from empty? Confirm no visible control navigates to ?empty=1.
unstated.fine_answers: ?empty=1 always starts with no messages and @Scribe still works there; it may apply only to that load or keep its own session state, and the room name may or may not be shown. A fresh session on / still starts from the seeded Launch plan room. Seeded messages shown under ?empty=1 are not fine.

unstated.text: What the empty-state guidance says and whether it goes away once the first message is sent.
unstated.why: Useful guidance should tell Maya how to start and how to call Scribe; guidance left on top of a real conversation is clutter.
unstated.probe: Open /?empty=1 and read the guidance (does it explain typing a message and mentioning @Scribe?). Send hello. Check whether the guidance is gone or reduced and the message shows as an article.
unstated.fine_answers: Any guidance that explains composing and mentioning @Scribe; it may be removed, reduced or kept after the first send, as long as the conversation stays readable.

unstated.text: The initial appearance: always light, or following the system's prefers-color-scheme, with a button label that matches the appearance shown.
unstated.why: A user with a dark system theme may get dark by default; the button must then say Use light appearance, or the label is wrong.
unstated.probe: In devtools emulate prefers-color-scheme: dark and open /; note the appearance and the button's label. Repeat with light.
unstated.fine_answers: Always start light (matching the light, Gemini-like look), or follow the system with a correct label. A dark start with the label Use dark appearance is not fine.

unstated.text: After Use light appearance switches back, the same button reads Use dark appearance again and the starting light appearance is restored, over repeated toggles.
unstated.why: The operator toggles more than once; a label that sticks or an appearance that drifts makes the control unreliable.
unstated.probe: Load / at 1440px; record the appearance and label. Activate the button three times, recording appearance and label after each.
unstated.fine_answers: The same button alternates between Use dark appearance and Use light appearance, with the starting light appearance restored each time. A second always-visible button was not asked for.

unstated.text: The appearance button stays visible and usable at 320px, 390px and 1440px widths.
unstated.why: The request requires a visible button and usable narrow layouts; a toggle hidden or pushed off-screen at 320px breaks both.
unstated.probe: At 320px, 390px and 1440px, load / and check the appearance button is visible and activatable without page-level horizontal scrolling; activate it at each width.
unstated.fine_answers: Visible and activatable at all three widths, including when it wraps to another line or sits in a compact header.

unstated.text: The dark appearance keeps text and controls readable: contrast of messages, timestamps, identity badges, the alert, and a visible focus indicator.
unstated.why: A dark mode with low-contrast timestamps or invisible focus rings makes reading and composing unusable for some users.
unstated.probe: Switch to dark, run a contrast check (Lighthouse or axe), and tab through Message, Send, the appearance button and Retry Scribe, checking the focus indicator is visible.
unstated.fine_answers: WCAG AA text contrast as the plain target and a visible focus indicator; the exact palette is open.

unstated.text: How a long unbroken token (a long URL or a 200-300 character word) and long multiline messages stay within the page at 320px, 390px and 1440px.
unstated.why: Pasted links and long tokens are ordinary in a project room and are what most often push the page sideways even when short messages fit.
unstated.probe: At 320px, send https://example.com/ followed by 300 letters with no spaces, and a 40-line message with several long lines. Check document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= the viewport width and that the full text is readable. Repeat at 390px and 1440px, and check Message and Send stay usable.
unstated.fine_answers: Breaking long words, or scrolling inside the message or Conversation region; no page-level horizontal scroll. Clipping text so it cannot be read is not fine.

unstated.text: The view scrolls to the newest message after Maya sends and after a Scribe reply arrives.
unstated.why: In a long conversation Maya should see what she just sent and the reply without hunting.
unstated.probe: On /, send ten messages so Conversation overflows, scroll up, then send @Scribe latest. Note whether the view shows the new message and then the reply.
unstated.fine_answers: Auto-scroll on own send and on reply, possibly only when already near the bottom; leaving the newest message off-screen with no indication is weak.

unstated.text: Keyboard focus stays on or returns to the Message textbox after sending.
unstated.why: Maya should keep typing without clicking back into the box.
unstated.probe: On /, type a message in Message and press Enter, then click Send for another; after each, check document.activeElement and type a character to see where it lands.
unstated.fine_answers: Focus stays on or returns to the Message textbox after Enter and after Send.

unstated.text: New messages and the Scribe reply are announced to screen-reader users (a live region), beyond the working state's role status.
unstated.why: A screen-reader user hears that Scribe is working but may not learn that the reply has arrived.
unstated.probe: With VoiceOver or NVDA on, send @Scribe hi and listen for the working state and then the reply or its arrival; or inspect the DOM for aria-live on Conversation or a status update on completion.
unstated.fine_answers: A polite live announcement of the reply, or the status region saying the reply arrived; either works.

unstated.text: How message times are shown: format, time zone, the times given to seeded messages (fixed or relative to now, and earlier than new messages), and whether they carry a machine-readable datetime.
unstated.why: A realistic seed with times in the future or in an odd format reads as broken; the operator cannot judge reading order, and a maintainer testing time rules needs predictable values.
unstated.probe: Open / and record each seeded article's time text; inspect for a <time datetime> element. Send a message and compare its time with the clock. Change the OS time zone, reload, and compare.
unstated.fine_answers: Local clock time, a date plus time, or a relative time, visible on each article; seeded times not later than new messages. Identical times on seed messages are fine.

unstated.text: Where newly sent messages appear relative to the seed and to each other (reading order).
unstated.why: The operator reads Launch plan's seed first and needs new messages to land in a predictable place.
unstated.probe: Read Conversation from start to end and record each seed article's author. Send first marker, then second marker; record where each appears relative to the seed and to each other.
unstated.fine_answers: Newest at the bottom or newest at the top, applied consistently; the seed may stay in its order above or below new messages.

unstated.text: Whether message length or the endpoint's request body size is limited.
unstated.why: A huge pasted text could freeze the page or make the server buffer an unbounded body; an operator would want a known ceiling.
unstated.probe: Send a 200,000-character message containing @Scribe and note whether the UI stays responsive and the reply arrives. curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/agent with a 50 MB JSON body and note the status and the server's memory.
unstated.fine_answers: No limit for a local demo is acceptable if large but sane messages work; a stated limit with a clear message (e.g. 413) is also fine. A crash is not fine.

unstated.text: Enter during IME composition (Japanese, Chinese input) does not send, and how a newline is entered on a mobile virtual keyboard.
unstated.why: Enter that confirms an IME candidate must not send a half-composed message; on a phone at 390px there is no Shift key.
unstated.probe: Enable a Japanese IME, type konnichiha in Message and press Enter to confirm the candidate; check nothing was sent. In a mobile emulator at 390px, check whether the return key sends or inserts a newline.
unstated.fine_answers: Enter during composition does not send; on mobile, the return key sending or inserting a newline are both acceptable.

unstated.text: How a maintainer runs the tests (node --test alone or an npm test script) and which Node.js version is needed.
unstated.why: The next maintainer needs the one command and the minimum Node version, since node:test and node --test discovery differ across versions.
unstated.probe: In the project folder run node --test and npm test; note results. Check package.json for scripts and engines and the README for run instructions.
unstated.fine_answers: node --test alone, or an npm test script wrapping it; a README line naming the command and a working Node version.

unstated.text: Scribe's demonstration-agent identity is visible on its articles (a label or badge such as Demo agent, not only hidden text), distinct from Maya and Theo shown as people.
unstated.why: The customer will demo this; an agent that looks like a person, or a bare bot label, undermines the stated clear identification.
unstated.probe: Open / and, for each seed article and any Scribe reply, record the visible author, the visible person/agent identity and the accessible name.
unstated.fine_answers: Visible wording such as demonstration agent or Demo agent, or an equally clear badge, on Scribe's articles; Maya and Theo read as people. A bare bot label is a weak match.

unstated.text: The seeded conversation reads as a coherent, realistic Launch plan discussion rather than placeholder text.
unstated.why: The customer will demo the seeded room; placeholder or incoherent text undermines it.
unstated.probe: Open / and read the seed from start to end; check the messages discuss planning a launch coherently and that no lorem ipsum or test strings appear.
unstated.fine_answers: Any coherent launch-planning exchange among Maya, Theo and Scribe.

unstated.text: Messages sent from the composer are attributed to Maya as a person, and there is no control to post as Theo or switch user.
